Mapping the Human Skills That Matter in the AI Era

Simone Maienfisch created a comprehensive framework of 24 skills that become more valuable — not less — as AI handles more of the execution.

By Chris O'Hara · November 2026 · 4 min read

As AI takes on more of the production work in product marketing, one question keeps surfacing: What should humans focus on? Simone Maienfisch has an answer — and it's now a core part of the NextGen PMM curriculum.

Simone Maienfisch

Global Vice President
SAP Cloud ERP Private and RISE Product Marketing

The Problem: AI Does More, But What Do Humans Do?

The conversation around AI in marketing often focuses on what AI can do — generate content, analyze data, personalize at scale. But Simone noticed a gap in the conversation: what should humans be getting better at while AI handles more execution?

"The skills in this framework are not new," Simone explains. "What's new is that working with AI amplifies their importance. As AI becomes better at generating information, humans get more value by framing, connecting, challenging, deciding, and governing the AI output."

Simone introduces the Human Soft Skills framework · 3 min

The Framework: 24 Skills Across 3 Categories

The Human Soft Skills Map identifies 24 capabilities that matter more — not less — in an AI-augmented workplace. They're organized into three categories:

🧠

Thinking

10 skills
🤝

Collaborate with AI

5 skills
💭

Mindset

9 skills

"Humans guide and decide what matters. AI produces content. It's always a plus+ — not AI or human."

— Simone Maienfisch

Thinking Skills: The Cognitive Foundation

These are the skills that help you guide AI effectively — synthesis, judgement, critical thinking. The "crown jewel" of the framework is metacognition: thinking about your own thinking.

10 Thinking Skills

  • Stakeholder Management
  • Systems Thinking
  • Synthesis
  • Decision Making
  • Judgement & Trade-offs
  • Fact Checking
  • Critical Thinking
  • Embed Policies
  • AI Ethics & Privacy
  • Metacognition ⭐

Why metacognition? Because AI can be biased, make incorrect assumptions, and reinforce existing beliefs — very confidently. AI agreeing with you doesn't mean you're right. The more AI becomes a thinking partner, the more important self-awareness becomes.

Collaborate with AI: The Practical Skills

These skills focus on the mechanics of working with AI effectively — from framing the right problem to iterating on outputs.

5 Collaboration Skills

  • Speed Reading / Info Triage
  • Context Building
  • Problem Framing
  • Asking Good Questions
  • Editing & Refinement

A key insight: "AI can solve wrong problems beautifully — but humans define the right problem." With AI, generating solutions becomes easier while defining the right problem becomes more critical.

Mindset: The Attitudes That Enable Success

Perhaps the most underrated category. These are the attitudes and approaches that determine whether someone thrives or struggles with AI collaboration.

9 Mindset Skills

  • Refinement Loops
  • AI Culture
  • Sustainability Awareness
  • Communication about AI
  • Human Creativity
  • Intellectual Humility
  • Curiosity
  • Cognitive Independence
  • Patience

Intellectual humility stands out: the willingness to be incorrect. AI confidently provides answers and tends to agree with you — which doesn't mean your viewpoint is right. Humans must remain open to being wrong.

From Framework to Curriculum

Simone's framework has become a core module in NextGen PMM, complete with an interactive skills map and self-assessment tool. Product marketers can now explore each skill, understand how it applies to AI collaboration, and assess their own development needs.

The framework answers a question many PMMs have been asking: "AI is doing more of my work — what should I be learning?" Now there's a structured answer.

The Bigger Picture

Simone's work reflects a broader shift in how we think about AI in the workplace. Rather than asking "What can AI do?" she asks "What should humans do?" The answer: guide, decide, challenge, verify, and create meaning.

As she puts it: "When AI increasingly generates, analyzes, recommends, and produces content — humans need to increasingly synthesize, judge, decide, verify, and create meaning."

That's a message worth spreading.
